extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in analytic/number theory; readers of the original Inventiones paper
extracted.subtask_description: An erratum to the research article 'The spin of prime ideals' giving corrected hypotheses and replacements in several displayed formulas and arguments; clarifies divisibility/coprimality conditions, modulus conventions (ideal vs integer), and the precise hypotheses under which Conjecture C_n may be applied. Intended to preserve the original results with minor proof modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: q does not divide m (weaker requirement than coprimality)
rubrics_metrics.description: On page 728 we claimed that q and m can be taken to be coprime. This is not always true but actually, in the application, we needed only that q does not divide m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace any use of the stronger 'q and m coprime' assumption by the weaker condition 'q ∤ m'. Consequence: all results remain unchanged aside from the listed proof modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the different 𝔇 factor in coefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: On page 723, line 2, replace 2^{2h+3}f by 2^{2h+3}f\,\mathfrak D, where \mathfrak D is the different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every occurrence of the omitted different in that coefficient must be multiplied in; this is a formal correction to the displayed factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 𝔤 and use of ideal modulus (replace 'mod q' by 'mod 𝔮')
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the first two lines following (6.21) by: '... where \mathfrak g takes from \mathfrak c all prime ideals of degree greater than one (recall that there are no ramified primes in \mathfrak c which is coprime to \mathfrak D), and all primes of degree one for which some different ...' and three lines later, in the congruence, replace 'mod q' by 'mod \mathfrak q'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ideal-theoretic modulus \mathfrak q (and the corresponding ideal-character notation) rather than the integer modulus q in the congruence statements; explicitly remove ramified primes from \mathfrak c because \mathfrak c is coprime to the different \mathfrak D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Conjecture C_n to incomplete character sums (modulus q = N\mathfrak q)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the modified congruence and progression argument: a runs over an arithmetic progression of modulus k dividing g_0 m F (with m = N\mathfrak m), so the inner sum can be arranged into n incomplete character sums of length << x^{1/n} and modulus q << x. Since χ_{\mathfrak q}(\ell) = (\ell/\mathfrak q) is the real primitive Dirichlet character of modulus q = N\mathfrak q, Conjecture C_n (or its arithmetic-progression consequence) applies, giving (see (9.4)) T(x;β) << g_0 x^{(1-δ)/n + ε}, except when q | k (and q | k implies q | m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjecture C_n may be applied under these exact structural conditions: n incomplete character sums, short length << x^{1/n}, modulus q bounded by << x, and the character being the real primitive character coming from the ideal \mathfrak q. The exceptional case q | k (equivalently q | m) must be handled separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: (6.25) holds if q ∤ m; exceptional condition (6.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace text so that (6.25) holds if q \not\mid m. Hence (6.25) fails only when the following holds: p | N(β - β') ⇒ p^2 | m F N(β - β'). (This is displayed as (6.26).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat (6.26) as the explicit exceptional criterion: primes dividing N(β-β') must, after multiplication by mF, become square factors. Outside this exceptional divisibility configuration, (6.25) is valid because q does not divide m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace 'squarefull' F^2N(...) conditions by conditional divisibility with factor mF
rubrics_metrics.description: In four subsequent displays, replace respectively: 'F^2N(β-β') squarefull' by 'p | N(β-β') ⇒ p^2 | m F N(β-β')'; 'F^2N(γ) squarefull' by 'p | N(γ) ⇒ p^2 | m F N(γ)'; 'F^2N\mathfrak b squarefull' by 'p | N\mathfrak b ⇒ p^2 | m F N\mathfrak b'; and 'F^2b squarefull' by 'p | b ⇒ p^2 | m F b'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the original argument invoked a 'squarefull' condition involving F^2, replace that notion by these conditional divisibility statements that incorporate the factor mF. Apply these replacements consistently in the four listed contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume m ≤ x (otherwise the sum is empty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert the sentence before (6.27): 'Note that we can assume m ≤ x else the sum in (6.1) is empty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bound m ≤ x to simplify or truncate summations; if m > x the relevant sum vanishes and requires no further estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace condition on N(γ) by divisibility g | N(γ)
rubrics_metrics.description: On page 730, change the third sentence after (6.33) to: '... The condition for N(γ) is now replaced by g | N(γ)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where previously a condition on N(γ) appeared, now require explicit divisibility by g; adjust subsequent arguments that used the old condition accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounds for S_χ(M,N;k,ℓ) valid for real primitive odd-modulus characters with q ∤ k
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the argument following (9.7): suppose χ = χ_q is real, primitive of odd modulus q (q is necessarily squarefree). For n = k m + ℓ one has χ(n) = χ_{(q,k)}(ℓ)·χ_{q/(q,k)}(k)·χ_{q/(q,k)}(m+r) with k r ≡ ℓ (mod q/(q,k)). It follows that the sum (9.7) is bounded by S_{χ_{q/(q,k)}}(M',N/k). Since the bound (9.4) does not depend on M, it remains valid for S_χ(M,N;k,ℓ) provided χ (mod q) is real, primitive with q odd and q \not\mid k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the decomposition of χ(n) when q is squarefree and odd; the key hypothesis for transferring the bound (9.4) to the twisted sum S_χ(M,N;k,ℓ) is that χ is real primitive of odd modulus and that q does not divide k. Handle the special cases where q | k separately.
